'''Janet Kear''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|OBE}} (13 January 1933 – 24 November 2004) was an [[England|English]] [[ornithologist]] and conservationist who worked extensively on waterfowl and wrote several major works on ducks. She was the first woman to become president of the [[British Ornithologists' Union|British Ornithologists' Union (BOU)]].
==Early life and education==
Kear was born in [[Middlesex]], the younger daughter of clerk Harold Kear and Constance May née Betteridge. Her brother David became a director-general of the New Zealand Department of Scientific and Industrial Research.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rees |first=Eileen C. |date=2005-10-01 |title=In Memoriam: Janet Kear, 1933–2004 |url=https://academic.oup.com/auk/article/122/4/1293/5562675 |journal=The Auk |volume=122 |issue=4 |pages=1293–1294 |doi=10.1093/auk/122.4.1293 |issn=1938-4254}}</ref> She was educated at [[Walthamstow Hall]], [[Sevenoaks]], Caspar Junior College, Wyoming, [[King's College London]] and then from 1956 [[Girton College, Cambridge]], where she obtained her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] on the feeding [[ecology]] of [[finch]]es in 1959 under [[Robert Hinde|Robert A. Hinde]]<ref>{{Cite news |title=Janet Kear |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/janet-kear-535026.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220707213232/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/janet-kear-535026.html |archive-date=7 July 2022 |access-date=2025-03-12 |work=The Independent |language=en-GB |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Unwin |first=Brian |date=2004-12-06 |title=Janet Kear |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2004/dec/06/obituaries.guardianobituaries |access-date=2025-03-12 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1959 Kear joined the staff of [[Peter Scott]]'s [[Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust]] at [[WWT Slimbridge|Slimbridge]], [[Gloucestershire]]. Her work included studies to breed Hawaiian goose and the reintroduction captive bred geese into the wild. She examined behaviour and development and made studies on geese grazing. She studied the health of waterfowl and methods for assessing them. From 1974 to 1977 she was the avicultural coordinator at WWT. She married [[Geoffrey Matthews|Geoffrey Vernon Townsend Matthews]], another researcher at the WWT, in 1964. They separated in 1978.<ref name=odnb />

In 1977 she became curator of the trust's new regional center at [[WWT Martin Mere|Martin Mere]], [[Lancashire]]. She met John Victor Turner, a volunteer ornithologist, whom she married in New Zealand in 1993. She was also known for having a lot of intercorrelations with many men.<ref name=odnb />

Kear was the first woman to become vice-president (1989–91), then president (1991–95) of the [[British Ornithologists' Union]], and edited their ''[[Ibis (journal)|Ibis]]'' magazine from 1980 to 1988. She authored more than 90 scientific papers.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Rees |first=Eileen C. |date=2005-10-01 |title=IN MEMORIAM: JANET KEAR, 1933–2004 |url=https://bioone.org/journals/the-auk/volume-122/issue-4/0004-8038_2005_122_1293_IMJK_2.0.CO_2/IN-MEMORIAM-JANET-KEAR-19332004/10.1642/0004-8038(2005)122[1293:IMJK]2.0.CO;2.full |journal=The Auk |volume=122 |issue=4 |pages=1293–1294 |doi=10.1642/0004-8038(2005)122[1293:IMJK]2.0.CO;2 |s2cid=85591370 |issn=0004-8038|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Her books included ''The Mute Swan'' (1989), ''Man And Wildfowl'' (1990) and ''Ducks of the World'' (1991). Kear was made a fellow of Liverpool University (1978–92) and an honorary doctorate with the title of professor from John Moores University in 1990. She received the [[Union Medal of the British Ornithological Union|British Ornithologists' Union's medal]] in 1998. She was awarded the [[Order of the British Empire]] in 1993.<ref name=odnb>{{cite ODNB|author=Rees, Eileen Rees|chapter= Kear, Janet (1933–2004)|title= Oxford Dictionary of National Biography| year=2008| doi=10.1093/ref:odnb/94353 }}</ref>

==Death and legacy==
Kear died in 2004. At the time of her death, she was working on a biography of the early medieval saint [[Werburgh]], who had an affinity with geese and is famous for bringing a goose back from the dead.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Helm|first=Christopher|date=2004|title=Obituary: Janet Kear OBE, 1933-2004|journal=Ibis|volume=147|pages=441–442|doi=10.1111/j.1474-919x.2005.00435.x |doi-access=free}}</ref>

From 2019, the BOU's redesigned Union Medal was renamed the "Janet Kear Union Medal", in her honour.<ref name="JKUM">{{cite web |title=The Janet Kear Union Medal |url=https://www.bou.org.uk/blog-janet-kear-union-medal/ |publisher=British Ornithologists' Union |access-date=10 September 2019 |date=28 May 2019}}</ref>
